summary: Post-market review: US equities diverged today. Total risk score 43.17 (caution), regime goldilocks, model confidence 0.911. The macro dimension led at 63.2, driven by the 2.45% real rate (99.44th percentile) and the 4.79% 10-year yield. August payrolls added 162 (vs 21 expected); the 2-year yield rose to 4.39%, Fed funds futures imply 3.94, and policy leans hike. Memory and equipment led (MU +5.04%, semiconductor equipment +4.72%, memory +5.04%), but autos -5.96% and AI software weakened; TSLA fell on a soft Cybercab and a regulatory probe. Crypto pulled back (BTC -2.04%, SOL -3.32%) and A-share memory/semis fell (603986.SH -2.95%, 301308.SZ -3.51%). VIX 14.32 stayed low, supporting the goldilocks regime, but breadth is weak.

top_risk_drivers.claim: August payrolls of 162 (vs 21 expected) reshaped the hike path; the 2-year yield rose to 4.39% (multi-year high), Fed funds futures imply 3.94, and policy leans hike; the 2.45% real rate at the 99.44th percentile leaves the macro dimension at 63.2, the model's highest.
Leadership is narrow: memory +5.04% and semiconductor equipment +4.72% led, but autos -5.96%, AI software -3.75% and crypto -2.04% weakened; cross-asset confirmation is only 0.5 and breadth is thin.
TSLA fell -5.96% on a disappointing Cybercab update and a US safety probe into nearly 1000 Cybercabs, dragging the auto theme to -5.96%.
A-share memory and semis fell against the US semiconductor rally (603986.SH -2.95%, 301308.SZ -3.51%), a divergence that reflects domestic-demand and geopolitical pressure.

supporting_signals.claim: Volatility stayed low, with VIX 14.32 (from 15.2) and realized vol 8.13, supporting the goldilocks regime; model confidence is 0.911.
The AI hardware theme continued: MU +5.04%, memory +5.04%, semiconductor equipment +4.72%, AMD +3.57%, AI infrastructure +3.55%, and NVDA +0.63% defended its open-ecosystem Hugging Face narrative.
Inflation kept cooling: CPI 3.30% (from 3.46%), core CPI 2.47%, PCE 3.34%, with breakevens anchored (5-year 2.33%, 10-year 2.35%).

contradicting_signals.claim: Mixed signals: August payrolls of 162 (vs 21) ran hot, yet CPI 3.30% and PCE 3.34% ran cool, leaving policy direction unclear — Fed funds futures imply a hike while inflation data argue for cuts.
Breadth not confirmed: cross-asset confirmation is only 0.5 and semis relative strength is -8.47, showing the goldilocks regime rests on a few leaders rather than broad participation.

what_changed_today: August payrolls of 162 (vs 21 expected) reshaped the hike path and the 2-year yield rose to 4.39%.
TSLA -5.96% fell on a soft Cybercab and a US regulatory probe, taking autos to -5.96%.
Memory and semiconductor equipment led (MU +5.04%, semiconductor equipment +4.72%) as the AI hardware theme continued.
Crypto pulled back (BTC -2.04%, SOL -3.32%) and A-share memory/semis fell (603986.SH -2.95%, 301308.SZ -3.51%).
watch_next: Watch next week's CPI (2026-09-11) and PPI (2026-09-10): Wall Street calls them decisive for whether September hikes.
Track the 2-year yield and the Fed funds futures implied rate of 3.94: if a hike lands, the 2.45% real rate tightens further.
Watch the TSLA probe, ADBE earnings (2026-09-10), and whether A-share memory/semis stop falling (603986.SH, 301308.SZ).

bull_case.title: Bull case: goldilocks persists as cooling inflation supports risk appetite
points: CPI 3.30% and core CPI 2.47% keep cooling; a soft CPI next week (2026-09-11) would fade hike odds and ease yields.
Memory and semiconductor equipment momentum continues (MU +5.04%, semiconductor equipment +4.72%) as the AI hardware theme broadens.

base_case.title: Base case: caution holds amid divergent signals
points: Hot jobs (162) and cool inflation (CPI 3.30%) coexist, the Fed path is uncertain, and markets range-trade.
Leadership is narrow (memory +5.04%, autos -5.96%) and breadth is thin, so the goldilocks regime is fragile.

bear_case.title: Bear case: hawkish surprise and risk spillover
points: Hot jobs plus sticky CPI force a hike; the 2.45% real rate (99.44th percentile) tightens further and pressures valuations.
The TSLA probe and crypto pullback (BTC -2.04%, SOL -3.32%) spread into a broader de-rating, with A-share weakness spilling over.
